title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
description: 《爱丽丝梦游仙境》是英国著名作家刘易斯·卡罗尔于 1865 年出版的奇幻荒诞文学代表作。本文件收录了全书完整的 12 个章节。故事讲述了小女孩爱丽丝在野外追逐一只怀抱怀表、会说话的白兔时，不慎掉入了一个神奇的兔子洞。在地下奇幻世界里，她通过喝药水、吃蛋糕身体奇妙地变大变小，遇到了会隐身的柴郡猫、疯狂的帽匠与三月兔、吸水烟的毛毛虫以及动辄要砍人头的红心王后。小说语言诙谐双关，充满荒诞逻辑与数学双关，是学习英国幽默与经典童话表达的至佳范本。

paragraphs.en: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it, 'and what is the use of a book,' thought Alice 'without pictures or conversations?' So she was considering in her own mind whether the pleasure of making a daisy-chain would be worth the trouble of getting up and picking the daisies, when suddenly a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝开始对坐在河岸边姐姐身旁且无事可做感到非常厌烦：有一两次她曾偷看姐姐正在阅读的书，但书里没有图片也没有对话，“一本没有图片也没有对话的书，”爱丽丝想，“有什么用呢？”因此她在自己心里盘算着做一条雏菊花环的乐趣是否值得站起来去摘雏菊的麻烦，这时突然一只长着粉红色眼睛的白兔在她身边跑过。

paragraphs.en: There was nothing so VERY remarkable in that; nor did Alice think it so VERY much out of the way to hear the Rabbit say to itself, 'Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!' But when the Rabbit actually took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet, for it flashed across her mind that she had never before seen a rabbit with either a waistcoat-pocket, or a watch to take out of it. Burning with curiosity, she ran across the field after it, and fortunately was just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge.
paragraphs.zh: 那并没有什么非常值得注意的；爱丽丝听到兔子自言自语说“天哪！天哪！我要迟到了！”也并没有觉得非常离谱。但当兔子居然从它的马甲口袋里掏出一块怀表并看了看，然后赶路时，爱丽丝跳了起来，因为在她脑海中闪过一个念头：她以前从未见过一只带着马甲口袋或者能从中掏出怀表的兔子。燃烧着好奇心，她穿过田野追赶它，幸运的是正好赶上看它钻进了篱笆下方的一个大兔子洞。

paragraphs.en: In another moment down went Alice after it, never once considering how in the world she was to get out again. The rabbit-hole went straight on like a tunnel for some way, and then dipped suddenly down, so suddenly that Alice had not a moment to think about stopping herself before she found herself falling down a very deep well.
paragraphs.zh: 在另一个时刻，爱丽丝追着它掉了下去，从来没有考虑过究竟如何再出来。兔子洞像一条隧道一样直直延伸了一段距离，然后突然向下俯冲，俯冲得如此突然以至于爱丽丝还没有来得急思考阻止自己，就发现自己正掉入一口非常深的井中。

paragraphs.en: Either the well was very deep, or she fell very slowly, for she had plenty of time as she went down to look about her and to wonder what was going to happen next. First, she tried to look down and make out what she was coming to, but it was too dark to see anything; then she looked at the sides of the well, and noticed that they were filled with cupboards and book-shelves; here and there she saw maps and pictures hung upon pegs. Down, down, down. Would the fall NEVER come to an end?
paragraphs.zh: 要么是井非常深，要么是她掉得非常慢，因为在下降时她有足够的时间环顾四周并好奇接下来会发生什么。首先，她试图向下看去辨认自己要到达哪里，但太暗了什么也看不见；接着她看了看井的侧面，注意到上面装满了碗橱和书架；到处她看到悬挂在钉子上的地图与图画。向下，向下，向下。难道坠落永远不会结束吗？

paragraphs.en: Down, down, down. There was nothing else to do, so Alice soon began talking again. 'Dinah'll miss me very much to-night, I should think!' (Dinah was the cat.) 'I hope they'll remember her saucer of milk at tea-time. Dinah my dear! I wish you were down here with me! There are no mice in the air, I'm afraid, but you might catch a bat, and that's very like a mouse, you know. But do cats eat bats, I wonder?' And here Alice began to get rather sleepy, and went on saying to herself, in a dreamy sort of way, 'Do cats eat bats? Do cats eat bats?' and sometimes, 'Do bats eat cats?' for, you see, as she couldn't answer either question, it didn't much matter which way she put it.
paragraphs.zh: 向下，向下，向下。没有什么别的事可做，因此爱丽丝很快又开始说话了。“我想今晚狄娜会非常想念我的！”（狄娜是那只猫。）“我希望他们在喝茶时间会记得她的那碟牛奶。我亲爱的狄娜！我希望你和我一起在这里！恐怕空气里没有老鼠，但你可能会抓到一只蝙蝠，你知道，那极其像老鼠。但猫吃蝙蝠吗，我好奇？”说到这里爱丽丝开始相当困倦了，并以一种梦幻般的方式继续对自己说：“猫吃蝙蝠吗？猫吃蝙蝠吗？”有时又说：“蝙蝠吃猫吗？”因为，你看，既然她哪个问题也回答不上来，她怎么问也就无所谓了。

paragraphs.en: 'Curiouser and curiouser!' cried Alice (she was so much surprised, that for the moment she quite forgot how to speak good English); 'now I'm opening out like the largest telescope that ever was! Good-bye, feet!' (for when she looked down at her feet, they seemed to be almost out of sight, they were getting so far off). 'Oh, my poor little feet, I wonder who will put on your shoes and stockings for you now, dears? I'm sure I shan't be able! I shall be a great deal too far off to trouble myself about you.'
paragraphs.zh: “越来越神奇，越来越稀奇了！”爱丽丝喊道（她太吃惊了，以至于有一瞬间她完全忘记了如何说正统的英语）；“现在我像有史以来最大的望远镜一样张开了！再见，脚们！”（因为当她向下看她的脚时，它们似乎几乎超出了视线，它们变得那么远）。“哦，我可怜的小脚们，我好奇现在谁会为你们穿上鞋袜呢，亲爱的？我确定我做不到了！我会远得根本顾不上关照你们了。”

paragraphs.en: Just then her head struck against the roof of the hall: in fact she was now more than nine feet high, and she at once took up the little golden key and hurried off to the garden door. Poor Alice! It was as much as she could do, lying down on one side, to look through into the garden with one eye; but to get through was more hopeless than ever: she sat down and began to cry again.
paragraphs.zh: 就在那时她的头撞到了大厅的屋顶：事实上她现在有九英尺多高了，她立刻拿起了小金钥匙急忙奔向花园门。可怜的爱丽丝！她所能做的一切就是侧身躺下，用一只眼睛透过去看花园；但要穿过去比以往任何时候都更加没有希望：她坐了下来，重新开始哭泣。

paragraphs.en: 'You ought to be ashamed of yourself,' said Alice, 'a great girl like you,' (she might well say this), 'to go on crying in this way! Stop this moment, I tell you!' But she went on all the same, shedding gallons of tears, until there was a large pool all round her, about four inches deep and reaching half down the hall.
paragraphs.zh: “你应该为你自己感到羞愧，”爱丽丝说，“像你这么大的女孩，”（她确实可以说这个），“以这种方式继续哭泣！这一刻给我停止，我告诉你！”但她依然照样哭着，流下了几加仑的眼泪，直到在她周围形成了一个大水塘，大约四英寸深，延伸到了大厅的中途。

paragraphs.en: After a time she heard a little pattering of feet in the distance, and she hastily dried her eyes to see what was coming. It was the White Rabbit returning, splendidly dressed, with a pair of white kid gloves in one hand and a large fan in the other: he came trotting along in a great hurry, muttering to himself as he came, 'Oh! the Duchess, the Duchess! Oh! won't she be savage if I've kept her waiting!'
paragraphs.zh: 过了一段时间，她听到远处有小脚步声，她急忙擦干眼睛看是什么过来了。那是白兔返回了，穿着极其华丽，一只手拿着一对白羊皮手套，另一只手拿着一把大扇子：他极其匆忙地小跑着过来，边走边自言自语：“哦！公爵夫人，公爵夫人！哦！如果我让她久等了，她难道不会发野蛮脾气吗！”

paragraphs.en: Alice felt so desperate that she was ready to ask help of any one; so, when the Rabbit came near her, she began, in a low, timid voice, 'If you please, sir—' The Rabbit started violently, dropped the white kid gloves and the fan, and skurried away into the darkness as hard as he could go.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝感到如此绝望，以至于她准备向任何人寻求帮助；因此，当兔子靠近她时，她用低沉、怯生生的声音开始说：“请问，先生——”兔子猛烈地吓了一跳，扔下了白羊皮手套和扇子，尽其所能拼命溜进了黑暗中。

chapters.title: Chapter 3: A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 3 章：无结果的赛跑与长尾巴故事

paragraphs.en: They were indeed a queer-looking party that assembled on the bank—the birds with draggled feathers, the animals with their fur clinging close to them, and all dripping wet, cross, and uncomfortable. The first question of course was, how to get dry again: they had a consultation about this, and after a few minutes it seemed quite natural to Alice to find herself talking me familiarly with them, as if she had known them all her life.
paragraphs.zh: 聚集在河岸上的确实是一群外表古怪的队伍——羽毛耷拉着的鸟类，毛发紧贴着身体的动物，全都浑身滴水、发脾气且不舒服。第一个问题当然是如何再次变干：他们对此进行了商讨，几分钟后爱丽丝发现自己极其熟悉地与他们交谈着，似乎她一辈子都认识他们一样自然。

paragraphs.en: At last the Dodo said, 'Everybody has won, and all must have prizes.' 'But who is to give the prizes?' quite a chorus of voices asked. 'Why, HER, of course,' said the Dodo, pointing to Alice with one finger; and the whole party at once crowded round her, calling out in a confused way, 'Prizes! Prizes!'
paragraphs.zh: 终于渡渡鸟说：“每个人都赢了，所有人必须有奖品。”“但谁给奖品呢？”齐声的声音合唱着问。“哎呀，当然是她了，”渡渡鸟说，用一只手指指着爱丽丝；整个队伍立刻拥挤在她周围，乱七八糟地喊着：“奖品！奖品！”

paragraphs.en: Alice had no idea what to do, and in despair she put her hand in her pocket, and pulled out a box of comfits, (fortunately the salt water had not got into it), and handed them round as prizes. There was exactly one a-piece all round. 'But she must have a prize herself, you know,' said the Lory. 'Of course,' the Dodo replied very gravely. 'What else have you got in your pocket?' he went on, turning to Alice. 'Only a thimble,' said Alice sadly. 'Hand it over here,' said the Dodo.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝不知道该怎么办，在绝望中她把手伸进口袋，掏出了一盒糖果（幸运的是盐水没有进到里面去），并把它们分发一圈作为奖品。正好每人有一颗。“但她自己也必须有一个奖品，你知道，”鹦鹉说。“当然，”渡渡鸟极其庄严地回答。“你口袋里还有什么东西？”他继续问，转向爱丽丝。“只有一个顶针，”爱丽丝悲伤地说。“拿过来，”渡渡鸟说。

paragraphs.en: Then they all crowded round her once more, while the Dodo solemnly presented the thimble, saying 'We beg your acceptance of this elegant thimble;' and, when it had finished this short speech, they all cheered. Alice thought the whole thing very absurd, but they all looked so grave that she did not dare to laugh.
paragraphs.zh: 接着他们所有人再次拥挤在她周围，渡渡鸟庄严地呈递上顶针，说：“我们请求您接受这枚高雅的顶针；”而当它讲完这番简短的演讲时，他们全都欢呼起来。爱丽丝认为整件事极其荒诞，但他们看起来全都是那么庄严，以至于她不敢笑出声。

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Rabbit Sends in a Little Bill
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 4 章：兔子派来了小比尔

paragraphs.en: It was the White Rabbit, trotting slowly back again, and looking anxiously about as it went, as if it had lost something; and she heard it muttering to itself 'The Duchess! The Duchess! Oh my dear paws! Oh my fur and whiskers! She'll get me executed, as sure as ferrets are ferrets! Where CAN I have dropped them, I wonder?'
paragraphs.zh: 那是白兔，慢慢地小跑着回来，边走边焦急地环顾四周，就仿佛他遗失了什么东西；她听到他对自己嘟囔着：“公爵夫人！公爵夫人！哦我亲爱的爪子！哦我的毛发和胡须！她会把我处决的，就像雪鼬就是雪鼬一样确定！我究竟能把它们掉在了哪里，我好奇？”

paragraphs.en: Alice guessed in a moment that it was looking for the fan and the pair of white kid gloves, and she very good-naturedly began hunting about for them, but they were nowhere to be seen—everything seemed to have changed since her swim in the pool, and the great hall, with the glass table and the little door, had vanished completely.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝瞬间猜到他在寻找扇子和那对白羊皮手套，她非常脾气好地开始到处寻找它们，但哪里也看不见它们——自从她在水塘里游过之后一切似乎都改变了，带有玻璃桌和小门的大厅已经完全消失了。

paragraphs.en: Very soon the Rabbit noticed Alice, as she went hunting about, and called out to her in an angry tone, 'Why, Mary Ann, what ARE you doing out here? Run home this moment, and fetch me a pair of gloves and a fan! Quick, now!' And Alice was so much frightened that she ran off at once in the direction it pointed to, without trying to explain the mistake it had made.
paragraphs.zh: 很快兔子注意到了爱丽丝（在她到处寻找时），并用愤怒的语气冲她喊：“哎呀，玛丽·安，你在外面干什么？这一刻跑回家去，给我取一对手套和一把扇子！现在快点！”爱丽丝极其害怕，以至于她立刻朝他指的方向跑去，没有试图解释他犯下的错误。

paragraphs.en: She ran till she came to a neat little house, on the door of which was a bright brass plate with the name 'W. RABBIT' engraved upon it. She went in without knocking, and hurried upstairs, in great fear lest she should meet the real Mary Ann and be turned out of the house before she had found the fan and gloves.
paragraphs.zh: 她跑着直到来到一栋整洁的小房子前，门上有一个闪亮的黄铜门牌，刻着名字“W·兔子”。她没有敲门就进去了，急忙上楼，非常害怕会遇到真正的玛丽·安，并在她找到扇子和手套前被赶出房子。

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Advice from a Caterpillar
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 5 章：毛毛虫的忠告

paragraphs.en: The Caterpillar and Alice looked at each other for some time in silence: at last the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth, and addressed her in a languid, sleepy voice. 'Who are YOU?' said the Caterpillar. This was not an encouraging opening for a conversation. Alice replied, rather shyly, 'I—I hardly know, sir, just at present—at least I know who I WAS when I got up this morning, but I think I must have been changed several times since then.'
paragraphs.zh: 毛毛虫和爱丽丝沉默地互相看了好一段时间：终于毛毛虫从嘴里拿开水烟袋，用一种倦怠、昏昏欲睡的声音向她开口。“你是谁？”毛毛虫说。对于一场对话来说这不是一个令人鼓励的开端。爱丽丝相当害羞地回答：“我——我目前几乎不知道，先生——至少我知道今天早上起床时我是谁，但我认为从那以后我肯定被改变了好几次了。”

paragraphs.en: 'What do you mean by that?' said the Caterpillar sternly. 'Explain yourself!' 'I can't explain MYSELF, I'm afraid, sir,' said Alice, 'because I'm not myself, you see.' 'I don't see,' said the Caterpillar. 'I'm afraid I can't put it more clearly,' Alice replied very politely, 'for I can't understand it myself to begin with; and being so many different sizes in a day is very confusing.'
paragraphs.zh: “你那样说是什么意思？”毛毛虫严厉地说。“解释你自己！”“恐怕我无法解释我自己，先生，”爱丽丝说，“因为我不是我自己了，你看。”“我看不到，”毛毛虫说。“恐怕我无法说得更清楚了，”爱丽丝极其礼貌地回答，“因为首先我自己就无法理解它；而一天里变那么多种不同的尺寸极其令人困惑。”

paragraphs.en: 'It isn't,' said the Caterpillar. 'Well, perhaps you haven't found it so yet,' said Alice; 'but when you have to turn into a chrysalis—you will some day, you know—and then after that into a butterfly, I should think you'll feel it a little queer, won't you?' 'Not a bit,' said the Caterpillar. 'Well, perhaps your feelings may be different,' said Alice; 'all I know is, it would feel very queer to ME.'
paragraphs.zh: “并不困惑，”毛毛虫说。“好吧，或许你还没有觉得如此，”爱丽丝说；“但当你不得不变成蛹时（你知道有一天你会的），接着在那之后变成蝴蝶，我想你会觉得有点古怪，难道不会吗？”“一点也不古怪，”毛毛虫说。“好吧，或许你的感受可能不同，”爱丽丝说；“我所知道的一切是，对我来说那会感觉极其古怪。”

paragraphs.en: In a minute or two the Caterpillar got down off the mushroom, and crawled away into the grass, merely remarking as it went, 'One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.' 'One side of WHAT? The other side of WHAT?' thought Alice to herself. 'Of the mushroom,' said the Caterpillar, just as if she had asked it aloud; and in another moment it was out of sight.
paragraphs.zh: 一两分钟内毛毛虫从蘑菇上爬了下来，爬进了草丛里，在走的时候仅仅注意到：“一边会让你长高，另一边会让你变矮。”“什么的一边？另一个的一边？”爱丽丝在心里想。“蘑菇的，”毛毛虫说，正好就像是她大声问出来了一样；在另一个时刻它已经脱离了视线。

paragraphs.en: For a minute or two she stood looking at the house, and wondering what to do next, when suddenly a footman in livery came running out of the wood—(she considered him to be a footman because he was in livery: otherwise, judging by his face only, she would have called him a fish)—and rapped loudly at the door with his knuckles. It was opened by another footman in livery, with a round face, and large eyes like a frog.
paragraphs.zh: 有一两分钟她站在那里看着房子，好奇接下来干什么，这时突然一个穿着仆役制服的男仆从树林里跑了出来（她认为他是一个男仆因为他穿着制服：否则，单凭他的脸判断，她会称他为一条鱼），用他的手指关节猛烈敲打门。门被另一个穿着制服的男仆打开了，带着圆脸和像青蛙一样的大眼睛。

paragraphs.en: The Fish-Footman began by producing from under his arm a great letter, nearly as large as himself, and this he handed over to the other, saying, in a solemn tone, 'For the Duchess. An invitation from the Queen to play croquet.' The Frog-Footman repeated, in the same solemn tone, only changing the order of the words a little, 'From the Queen. An invitation for the Duchess to play croquet.' Then they both bowed low, and their curls got entangled together.
paragraphs.zh: 鱼男仆首先从他的手臂下拿出一封大信，几乎和他自己一样大，他把它交给了另一个，用庄严的语气说：“给公爵夫人。来自王后打槌球的邀请。”青蛙男仆重复着，用同样庄严的语气，仅仅稍微改变了一下词语的顺序：“来自王后。给公爵夫人打槌球的邀请。”接着他们两个低头深深鞠躬，他们的卷发缠在了一起。

paragraphs.en: Alice laughed so much at this, that she had to run back into the wood for fear of their hearing her; and when she next peeped out the Fish-Footman was gone, and the other was sitting on the ground near the door, staring stupidly up into the sky. Alice went timidly up to the door, and knocked.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝对此笑了那么多，以至于她不得不跑回树林里害怕他们听到她；而当她下一次偷看时，鱼男仆已经走了，另一个正坐在门附近的地面上，愚蠢地仰望着天空。爱丽丝怯生生地走到门前，敲了敲门。

paragraphs.en: 'There's no sort of use in knocking,' said the Footman, 'and that for two reasons. First, because I'm on the same side of the door as you are; secondly, because they're making such a noise inside, no one could possibly hear you.' And certainly there was a most extraordinary noise going on within—a constant howling and sneezing, and every now and then a great crash, as if a dish or kettle had been broken to pieces.
paragraphs.zh: “敲门没有任何用处，”男仆说，“而且有两个原因。首先，因为我和你在门的同一侧；其次，因为他们在里面制造着那么大的噪音，没有人可能听到你。”确实里面正在进行着最非凡的噪音——持续的号啕与打喷嚏，隔三岔五一声巨大的破碎声，就仿佛盘子或水壶被打成了碎片。

chapters.title: Chapter 7: A Mad Tea-Party
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 7 章：疯帽客的茶会

paragraphs.en: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house, and the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep, and the other two were using it as a cushion, resting their elbows on it, and talking over its head. 'Very uncomfortable for the Dormouse,' thought Alice; 'only, as it's asleep, I suppose it doesn't mind.'
paragraphs.zh: 在房子前面的树下摆着一张桌子，三月兔和帽匠正在桌前喝茶：一只睡鼠坐在他们中间，熟睡着，另外两个把它用作靠垫，把肘部搁在它上面，在它的头上交谈着。“对睡鼠来说极其不舒服，”爱丽丝想；“不过，既然它睡着了，我想它不介意。”

paragraphs.en: The table was a large one, but the three were all crowded together at one corner of it: 'No room! No room!' they cried out when they saw Alice coming. 'There's PLENTY of room!' said Alice indignantly, and she sat down in a large arm-chair at one end of the table.
paragraphs.zh: 桌子是一张大桌子，但三个人全都拥挤在它的一角：“没有地方！没有地方！”当他们看到爱丽丝过来时他们喊道。“有大量的地方！”爱丽丝愤慨地说，并在桌子一头的一张大扶手椅上坐了下来。

paragraphs.en: 'Have some wine,' the March Hare said in an encouraging tone. Alice looked all round the table, but there was nothing on it but tea. 'I don't see any wine,' she remarked. 'There isn't any,' said the March Hare. 'Then it wasn't very civil of you to offer it,' said Alice angrily. 'It wasn't very civil of you to sit down without being invited,' said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: “喝点酒吧，”三月兔用鼓励的语气说。爱丽丝环顾桌子四周，但上面除了茶之外什么也没有。“我没看到任何酒，”她注意到。“没有任何酒，”三月兔说。“那么你提议请喝它不是很礼貌，”爱丽丝生气地说。“你没有被邀请就坐下来不是很礼貌，”三月兔说。

paragraphs.en: 'I didn't know it was YOUR table,' said Alice; 'it's laid for a great many more than three.' 'Your hair wants cutting,' said the Hatter. He had been looking at Alice for some time with great curiosity, and this was his first speech. 'You should learn not to make personal remarks,' Alice said with some severity; 'it's very rude.'
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道那是你的桌子，”爱丽丝说；“它是为比三个人多得多的人摆设的。”“你的头发需要剪了，”帽匠说。他带着巨大的好奇心看了爱丽丝好一段时间，这是他的第一番演讲。“你应该学会不要做出人身攻击评论，”爱丽丝带着某种严厉说；“那极其粗鲁。”

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The Queen’s Croquet-Ground
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 8 章：王后的槌球场

paragraphs.en: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white, but there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red. Alice thought this a very curious thing, and she went near to watch them, and just as she came up to them she heard one of them say, 'Look out now, Five! Don't go splashing paint over me like that!'
paragraphs.zh: 一棵大玫瑰树立在花园入口附近：上面生长的玫瑰是白色的，但有三个园丁在它旁边，忙着把它们涂成红色。爱丽丝认为这是一件极其神奇的事，她走近观看他们，就在她走到他们跟前时她听到他们中的一个说：“现在小心，五号！别那样把油漆溅在我身上！”

paragraphs.en: 'I couldn't help it,' said Five, in a sulky tone; 'Seven jogged my elbow.' On which Seven looked up and said, 'That's right, Five! Always lay the blame on others!' 'YOU'D better not talk!' said Five. 'I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded!' 'What for?' said the one who had spoken first. 'That's none of YOUR business, Two!' said Seven.
paragraphs.zh: “我没办法，”五号用闷闷不乐的语气说；“七号碰了我的肘部。”对此七号抬头说：“对极了，五号！总是把责任推给别人！”“你最好别说话！”五号说。“我昨天刚听到王后说你该被斩首！”“为什么？”最先说话的那个人说。“那不关你的事，二号！”七号说。

paragraphs.en: Alice went up to them and asked softly, 'Would you tell me, please, why you are painting those roses?' Two began, in a low voice, 'Why, the fact is, you see, Miss, this here ought to have been a RED rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know. So you see, Miss, we're doing our best, afore she comes, to—' At this moment Five, who had been anxiously looking across the garden, called out 'The Queen! The Queen!' and the three gardeners instantly threw themselves flat upon their faces.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝走到他们跟前软软地问：“请你们告诉我，你们为什么在把那些玫瑰涂色？”二号用低沉的声音开始说：“哎呀，事实是，你看，小姐，这里本来应该是一棵红玫瑰树，我们错放了一棵白色的；如果王后发现了，我们都会被砍头的，你知道。所以你看，小姐，我们在她来之前尽最大努力去——”在这一时刻一直在焦急地向花园对面看的五号大喊：“王后！王后！”三个园丁立刻脸朝下平摊在了地上。

chapters.title: Chapter 9: The Mock Turtle’s Story
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 9 章：假海龟的故事

paragraphs.en: 'You can't think how glad I am to see you again, you dear old thing!' said the Duchess, as she tucked her arm affectionately into Alice's, and they walked off together. Alice was very glad to find her in such a pleasant temper, and thought to herself that perhaps it was only the pepper that had made her so savage when they met in the kitchen.
paragraphs.zh: “你无法想象再次见到你我是多么高兴，你这亲爱的老小伙！”公爵夫人说，同时她亲热地把手臂塞进爱丽丝的臂弯里，她们一起走了开去。爱丽丝极其高兴发现她处于这样愉快的脾气中，并在心里想或许仅仅是胡椒使她在厨房相遇时变得那么野蛮。

paragraphs.en: They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun. 'Up, lazy thing!' said the Queen, 'and take this young lady to see the Mock Turtle, and to hear his history. I must go back and see after some executions I me ordered;' and she walked off, leaving Alice alone with the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: 她们很快遇到了一只鹰头狮，正熟睡在太阳下。“起来，懒惰的东西！”王后说，“带这位年轻女士去见假海龟，并听听他的历史。我必须回去料理我命令的一些处决；”她走了开去，留下爱丽丝单独与鹰头狮在一起。

paragraphs.en: They had not gone far before they saw the Mock Turtle in the distance, sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock, and, as they came nearer, Alice could hear him sighing as if his heart would break. She pitied him deeply. 'What is his sorrow?' she asked the Gryphon, and the Gryphon answered, 'It's all his fancy, that: he hasn't got no sorrow, you know. Come on!'
paragraphs.zh: 她们没走多远就在远处看到了假海龟，悲伤而孤独地坐在岩石的小突出部上，而当她们靠近时，爱丽丝能听到他叹息着，就仿佛他的心要碎了一样。她深深地同情他。“他的悲伤是什么？”她问鹰头狮，鹰头狮回答：“那全是他的幻想，那：他没有任何悲伤，你知道。来吧！”

paragraphs.en: The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and drew the back of one flipper across his eyes. He looked at Alice, and tried to speak, but for a minute or two sobs choked his voice. 'Same as if he had a bone in his throat,' said the Gryphon: and it set to work shaking him and punching him in the back. At last the Mock Turtle recovered his voice, and, with tears running down his cheeks, he went on again.
paragraphs.zh: 假海龟深深叹息着，用一只鳍脚的背面擦过双眼。他看着爱丽丝，试图说话，但有一两分钟抽泣哽咽了他的声音。“就像是他的喉咙里卡了一根骨头，”鹰头狮说：它开始干活摇晃他并在背上重击他。终于假海龟恢复了他的声音，而随着眼泪沿着面颊流下，他再次继续了。

paragraphs.en: 'You may not have lived much under the sea,' ('I haven't,' said Alice)—'and perhaps you were never even introduced to a lobster—' (Alice began to say 'I once tasted—' but checked herself hastily, and said 'No, never')—'so you can have no idea what a delightful thing a Lobster Quadrille is!'
paragraphs.zh: “你可能没有在海底生活多久，”（“我没有，”爱丽丝说）“—而或许你甚至从未被介绍给一只龙虾—”（爱丽丝开始说“我曾经尝过—”但急忙制止了自己，说“不，从未”）“—因此你无法概念龙虾舞曲是一件多么令人愉快的东！”

paragraphs.en: 'No, indeed,' said Alice. 'What sort of a dance is it?' 'Why,' said the Gryphon, 'you first form into a line along the sea-shore—' 'Two lines!' cried the Mock Turtle. 'Seals, turtles, salmon, and so on; then, when you've cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way—' 'THAT generally takes some time,' interrupted the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，确实如此，”爱丽丝说。“那是什么样的舞蹈？”“哎呀，”鹰头狮说，“你首先沿着海岸排成一条线—”“两条线！”假海龟喊道。“海豹、海龟、三文鱼等等；接着，当你把所有的水母都从路上清理干净后—”“那通常需要一些时间，”鹰头狮打断道。

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Who Stole the Tarts?
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 11 章：谁偷了王后的馅饼？

paragraphs.en: The King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne when they arrived, with a great crowd assembled round them—all sorts of little birds and beasts, as well as the whole pack of cards: the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him; and near the King was the White Rabbit, with a trumpet in one hand, and a scroll of parchment in the other.
paragraphs.zh: 当她们到达时红心国王和王后正坐在他们的王座上，一大群人聚集在他们周围——各种各样的小鸟和小野兽，以及整副扑克牌：侍从站在他们面前，戴着锁链，每侧有一个士兵守卫着他；在国王附近是白兔，一只手拿着喇叭，另一只手拿着一卷羊皮纸。

paragraphs.en: In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it: they looked so good, that it made Alice quite hungry to look at them—'I wish they'd get the trial done,' she thought, 'and hand round the refreshments!' But there seemed to be no chance of this, so she began looking at everything about her, to pass away the time.
paragraphs.zh: 就在法庭的正中央有一张桌子，上面有一大盘馅饼：它们看起来那么好，以至于看着它们使爱丽丝相当饥饿——“我希望他们把审判搞定，”她想，“并分发点心！”但似乎没有这个机会，因此她开始看着她周围的一切，以消磨时间。

paragraphs.en: Alice had never been in a court of justice before, but she had read about them in books, and she was quite pleased to find that she knew the name of nearly everything there. 'That's the judge,' she said to herself, 'because of his great wig.' The judge, by the way, was the King; and as he wore his crown over the wig, he did not look at all comfortable, and it was certainly not becoming.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝以前从未去过法院，但她在书里阅读过关于它们的东西，她相当高兴发现她几乎知道那里一切东西的名字。“那是法官，”她对自己说，“因为他的假发。”顺便说一下，法官就是国王；而因为他在假发上面戴着皇冠，他看起来一点也不舒服，而且那肯定不合适。

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Alice’s Evidence and the Awakening
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 12 章：爱丽丝的证词与梦醒时分（全本终极结局）

paragraphs.en: 'Here!' cried Alice, jumping up in such a hurry that she knocked over the jury-box with the skirt of her dress, upsetting all the jurymen on to the heads of the crowd below, and there they lay sprawling about, reminding her very much of a globe of goldfish she had accidentally upset the week before.
paragraphs.zh: “到！”爱丽丝喊道，跳得那么急以至于她的裙摆推倒了陪审员席，把所有的陪审员都打翻到了下面人群的头上，他们躺在那里手忙脚乱，极大程度地提醒了她一周前她意外打翻的那缸金鱼。

paragraphs.en: 'Oh, I BEG your pardon!' she exclaimed in a tone of great dismay, and began picking them up again as quickly as she could, for the accident of the goldfish kept running in her head, and she had a vague sort of idea that they must be collected at once and put back into the jury-box, or they would die.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我请求您的原谅！”她用极度沮丧的语气惊呼，并开始尽可能快地重新捡起他们，因为金鱼的意外不断在她脑海中闪现，她有一种模糊的概念，他们必须立刻被收集起来并放回陪审员席，否则他们会死的。

paragraphs.en: 'The trial cannot proceed,' said the King in a very grave voice, 'until all the jurymen are back in their proper places—ALL,' he repeated with great emphasis, looking hard at Alice as he said so. Alice looked at the jury-box, and saw that, in her haste, she had put the Lizard in head downwards, and the poor little thing was waving its tail about in a melancholy way.
paragraphs.zh: “审判无法进行，”国王用极其庄严的声音说，“直到所有的陪审员都回到他们适当的位置——所有人，”他带着巨大的强调重复着，说话时狠狠瞪着爱丽丝。爱丽丝看着陪审员席，看到在她的仓促中，她把蜥蜴头朝下放了进去，可怜的小东西正以一种忧郁的方式摇晃着它的尾巴。

paragraphs.en: 'Off with her head!' screamed the Queen at the top of her voice. Nobody moved. 'Who cares for you?' said Alice, who had grown to her full size by this time. 'You're nothing but a pack of cards!' At this the whole pack rose up into the air, and came flying down upon her: she gave a little scream, half of fright and half of anger, and tried to beat them off, and found herself lying on the bank, with her head in the lap of her sister, who was gently brushing away some dead leaves that had fluttered down from the trees upon her face.
paragraphs.zh: “砍掉她的头！”王后用她最大的声音尖叫道。没人动弹。“谁在乎你们？”此时已经长到全尺寸的爱丽丝说。“你们只不过是一副扑克牌！”听到这个整副扑克牌升上高空，飞快降落砸向她：她发出一声小尖叫，一半是吓的一半是气，并试图打散它们，发现自己正躺在河岸边，头靠在姐姐的腿上，姐姐正在轻轻拂去一些从树上飘落到她脸上的干叶子。

paragraphs.en: 'Wake up, Alice dear!' said her sister. 'Why, what a long sleep you've had!' 'Oh, I've had such a curious dream!' said Alice, and she told her sister all these strange Adventures of hers that you have just been reading about. And her sister kissed her, and said, 'It WAS a curious dream, dear, certainly: but now run in to your tea; it's getting late.' So Alice got up and ran off, thinking while she ran, as well she might, what a wonderful dream it had been.
paragraphs.zh: “醒醒，亲爱的爱丽丝！”她的姐姐说。“哎呀，你睡了多么长的一觉啊！”“哦，我做了这样一个奇妙的梦！”爱丽丝说，并将她刚刚经历的所有这些神奇冒险告诉了她的姐姐。她的姐姐亲吻了她，说：“那确实是一个奇妙的梦，亲爱的，毫无疑问：但现在跑进去吃你的下午茶吧；时间变迟了。”于是爱丽丝站起来跑开了，一边跑一边想着，就像她应该的那样，那是多么美好的一场梦。
